findings.proposed: Use '#' in the four many arms: many {# de completadas}, many {# de fallidas}, many {# de detenidas}, many {# con estado desconocido}. Every other arm keeps the '::group-off' skeleton exactly as English.
findings.reason: The 'many' arms are es-authored (English has no category arms here) and exist because es CLDR puts exact millions in 'many' ('un millón de completadas'). Each one reuses the sibling arms' '::group-off' skeleton, so the only number that can reach it prints ungrouped: rendering completed=1000000 gives "1000000 de completadas". Spanish always groups, and the es style guide's own exemplar for this category is many {# de sesiones}, illustrated as "1.000.000 de sesiones". Verified: many {# de completadas} renders "1.000.000 de completadas". Real but unreachable in practice (>=1,000,000 requests in one sound batch), and a one-commit fix, hence MINOR rather than MAJOR.
findings.supplemental_evidence_disposition: Retained non-gating finding and original disposition unchanged. No new wording/semantics audit or edit; images do not adjudicate this language judgment.

findings.reason: This value is also the audio player's accessible name: media-label.ts documents it, and sound-player.tsx composes it into ui.chat.audio.play_label / pause_label / position_label, producing "Reproducir Sonido 2" — a capitalised common noun mid-sentence, an orthography error in Spanish. The visible tile/alt-text surface wants the capital ('Imagen' keeps it for the same reason); the composed accessible name wants lower case. Same trade-off the ru round-3 audit recorded as S16F-RU-R3-01.
